ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
One vertex of the triangle on the left is connected to one vertex of the triangle on the right using a straight line so that no connecting line segment dissects either of the two triangles into two parts. In how many ways is this possible?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two separated triangles, similar in shape, both wedge-shaped triangles with a sharp vertex on the left and a vertical side on the right. Label the three vertices of the left triangle as A (left sharp point), B (upper-right point), C (lower-right point); label the three vertices of the right triangle as D (left sharp point), E (upper-right point), F (lower-right point). Reasoning: Choose one vertex from the left triangle and one vertex from the right triangle, for a total of 3×3=9 ways to connect. If connecting from A to D, E, F, the line segment will pass through the interior of the left triangle from the left sharp point and then leave, so it will partition the left triangle, discard. B-D and C-D are located in the gap between the two triangles and do not partition either triangle, keep. B-E is an upper outside connection, and C-F is a lower outside connection, and they also do not partition a triangle, keep. B-F and C-E will pass through the interior of the right triangle, dividing the right triangle into two parts, discard. Therefore the feasible ways to connect are B-D, C-D, B-E, C-F, for a total of 4.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: there are two separated triangles, both shaped like wedges with a left-pointing vertex and a vertical side on the right. Label the left triangle's vertices as A = left point, B = upper right, C = lower right; label the right triangle's vertices as D = left point, E = upper right, F = lower right. From the text, we must choose one vertex from the left triangle and one from the right triangle and draw a straight segment, but the segment must not pass through the interior of either triangle in a way that splits it. Enumerate the 9 possible vertex pairs. Any segment starting at A and going to the right triangle passes through the interior of the left triangle before leaving it, so discard A-D, A-E, A-F. From B or C to D, the segment stays in the gap/outside both triangles and ends at the left point of the right triangle, so B-D and C-D are allowed. From B to E is an upper outside/tangent-type connection and from C to F is a lower outside/tangent-type connection, so both are allowed. The crossed connections B-F and C-E cut through the right triangle, so discard them. Thus the allowed connections are B-D, C-D, B-E, and C-F, giving 4 ways.
